newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian Metals - Copper seen moving to Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals - Copper seen moving to Singapore.

text.p: Far East base metal traders said on Friday up to 5,000 tonnes of copper will arrive shortly in Singapore from Shanghai and Hamburg while adding that prices in the London Metal Exchange (LME) may run into profit-taking.

"There's still material moving here," a dealer in a Western metal trading company told Reuters. "About 2,000 to 5,000 tonnes of copper is on its way to Singapore. It's a mix of material from Shanghai and Hamburg."
"I know that 5,000 tonnes is either on its way here or has already arrived," another trader in a Singapore-based metal trading firm said.

Copper stocks in the LME warehouse here reached a meagre 1,450 tonnes by the end of last month but have since risen to 8,225 tonnes by Tuesday, November 19. Stocks jumped by 5,500 tonnes on the previous Friday, November 15.
One trader estimated that up to 15,000 tonnes of copper have not been placed on warrant in Singapore with holders of the material plainly hoping for a further upward spike in prices on the LME.
Brokerage Rudolf Wolff said in its Evening Metal Report in London on Thursday that further increases in Singapore stocks could provide the impetus for "an aggressive bear raid" in the market.

"Prices have moved up too much, too fast," a dealer here said. "If the market comes down, it will come down very rapidly. I think it (three month copper prices) may slide all the way down to US$2,120 a tonne."

Traders here expect LME copper stocks to slide by 2,000 to 5,000 tonnes when its report is released at 0900 GMT. They also expect aluminium stocks to post a modest fall of about 500-1,000 tonnes in the report.
One trader, however, said copper stocks will be in a wide range, increasing by 2,000 tonnes or dropping by 5,000 tonnes.
"I think it will go down by that level," a dealer in a Japanese trading house said, refering to the consensus here of a fall in copper stocks of about 2,000-5,000 tonnes.
More material may move into LME warehouses with cash copper now being quoted at $2,350 a tonne, one dealer said.
"The prices are very attractive now," he said.
Three month copper prices were priced here at around $2,210/15 a tonne at 0300 GMT against the kerb close in London on Thursday of $2,212 a tonne and the late trade of $2,213 a tonne.
Three month aluminium prices were quoted at about $1,522/27 a tonne at 0300 GMT compared to the late trade yesterday in London of $1,518 a tonne, metal dealers said.
"Aluminium will run into strong resistance at $1,520/40. There will be a lot of producer selling if the price hits that level," the aluminium dealer of a Japanese trading company said.
Demand for zinc and lead around the region remained steady and is expected to pick up strongly, especially in the second half of 1997, traders said.

"We don't have enough zinc in the second half of 1997. There is a crunch coming," the zinc dealer for a Western metal company said, adding most of the demand will come from the rapidly growing economies of Asia. "The physical demand is also very good in the United States."

Copper premiums in Singapore eased sharply with the presence of more material in the city-state and primarily because of slack business here, dealers said. Premiums for other base metals followed suit.
Copper premiums were quoted at around $50-$80 a tonne after hovering at around $100 a tonne since the end of August.
"There's just not been a lot of business done lately," one dealer said.
